killed_party1_own_status_after_restart_o.note: party 1's own /stato stays stuck at 'in corso' forever for this request -- its worker died before it could ever update its own status. The backend still learns the request failed via party 0's callback/status, but querying party 1 directly (if it were ever brought back without clearing this key) would be misleading in isolation.

salute_gap_observed: party 1's own /salute continued reporting ok:true even while its worker container was dead -- /salute only checks Redis reachability and static file presence (binary, compiled program, certs), not whether the worker process is actually alive. A monitoring setup relying solely on /salute would not detect this failure mode.
